card.title: JÄGER BATTALION 2
card.text: Deployment: Add a SISSI to your support line.
card.flavorText: The 2nd Jäger Battalion was a unit of the Armored Division of the Finnish Army during the Continuation War (1941-1944). The division was formed in 1942 and consisted of a newly formed Armored Brigade and the elite Jaeger Brigade which was created in 1921. It is still active today. In 1944 the division also consisted of the 14th Heavy Artillery Battalion, 6th Signals Battalion, 2nd Pioneer Battalion and the Separate Armour Company which operated BT-42 assault guns. In addition to the many captured T-26 variants, the division also possessed a number of obsolete T-28s, a small number of captured T-34s armed with a 76mm cannon and 2 tanks of the hulking KV1 series. During the Continuation War, the Finnish Armored Division was mostly located at Petrozavodsk (which is now the Republic of Karelia in the Russian Federation) but in 1944 it was moved to the Karelian Isthmus. This year the division took part in the Battle of Kuuterselkä, the Battle of Tali-Ihantala and the Battle of Vuosalmi. In October 1944 it participated in the Lapland War and fought in the Battle of Rovaniemi against the German Twentieth Mountain Army. The Armored Division was disbanded during the Lapland War on 30 December 1944.
